newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products firm on stronger crudes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products firm on stronger crudes.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady to firmer on Friday along with higher crude prices, traders said.

They said gas oil prices were set to rise on increased regional demand especially from China, which is projected to import between 800,000 and 1.0 million tonnes for January arrival. They said China's insatiable demand is spilling into the Hong Kong barge market, where stocks are tightening sharply.
Traders said three gas oil cargoes were traded on Thursday between $32.20 and $32.40 a barrel for January fob Singapore, with two cargoes bound for China.

On Friday an offer of 195,000 barrels of gas oil were seen at $32.60, for Jan 14-18 lifting fob, with a bid seen at $32.40 for Jan 11-15. Gas oil swaps also rose with January traded at $32.20, up from $32.10 on Thursday.
Jet fuel also remained firm on sustained north Asian demand seen at over $2 a barrel premium to Singapore quotes c+f. Two bids for Jan 11-15 was seen at $33.80, with no offers seen.

Naphtha were steady and physical trading was thin as most players were still out of the market. On the swaps, January was quoted unchanged from Thursday at $24.50/$24.60 and was traded late Thursday at $24.56 a barrel.

The Indian Bombay 20,000-tonnes of low aromatic naphtha sell tender for lifting on January 6-8 was awarded to Itochu and traders said the price was at $22.50 below spot Japanese quotes on a free-on-board basis. Caltex Bahrain has issued a term tender to sell light naphtha (B210) for loading in the second half of 1997.The tender closes on Jan 3.

Fuel oil prices were assessed steady to firm on strong crude levels in thin talk. Traders said prices could face pressure near term as more Mideast supplies arrive by end January and in the face of dull Chinese demand which appeared to have come to a temporary halt. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
